--- pagetitle: "fmrimod" toc: false sidebar: false page-layout: full jupyter: python3 --- ::: {.hero} ::: {.hero-copy} [Python · fMRI modeling]{.eyebrow} # Typed, composable fMRI modeling. [From an event table to a first-level fit you can inspect at every step — HRFs, design matrices, contrasts, and group reductions as Python values, not opaque arrays.]{.lead} [Get started →](get-started.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [API reference](reference/index.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-secondary} [HRFs]{.kicker} [design matrices]{.kicker} [first-level GLM]{.kicker} [contrasts]{.kicker} ::: ::: {.hero-code} ::: {.code-card} [quickstart.py]{.code-card-title} ```python import fmrimod as fm from fmrimod.spec import hrf, drift from fmrimod.contrast import condition # The design is a typed value — compose with +, fit it directly. design = hrf("condition", basis="spmg1") + drift("poly", degree=2) fit = fm.fmri_lm(design, dataset) # The hypothesis names conditions, not column positions. faces = fit.contrast( condition("face", term="condition") - condition("scene", term="condition"), name="face_minus_scene", ) faces.estimate.round(2) # recovers the injected effect: ≈ 2.0 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## In 30 seconds {.promise-heading} A design in fmrimod is a **typed Python value**, not a magic string. You build it from `hrf(...)`, `drift(...)`, `intercept(...)` terms, compose them with `+`, and inspect every field before a single coefficient is solved. ::: {#e7dda52a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import pandas as pd import fmrimod as fm from fmrimod.spec import hrf, drift from fmrimod.contrast import condition events = pd.DataFrame({ "onset": np.arange(8, 210, 12.0), "condition": np.where(np.arange(17) % 2 == 0, "face", "scene"), "duration": 2.0, }) # Compose the design, then read its typed fields — no string parsing. design = hrf("condition", basis="spmg1") + drift("poly", degree=2) design.events[0].variables, design.events[0].hrf, design.baseline[0].basis ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (('condition',), 'spmg1', 'poly') ``` ::: ::: We use test data with a **known** face−scene effect of `2.0` in five of ten voxels, so the recovered number can be *checked*, not just inspected for shape. The dataset is built by `dataset_with_effect` — a tutorial-support helper that places the known effect on the column the **typed `condition(...)` object resolves to**, the same object the contrast below uses, never a rendered-name string lookup. ::: {#986c0f84 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} from fmrimod.simulate.demo import dataset_with_effect sampling = fm.SamplingFrame(blocklens=220, TR=1.0) dataset = dataset_with_effect( design, events, on=condition("face", term="condition"), effect=2.0, sampling_frame=sampling, seed=202, ) ``` ::: ::: {#34d9ed90 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fit = fm.fmri_lm(design, dataset) faces = fit.contrast( condition("face", term="condition") - condition("scene", term="condition"), name="face_minus_scene", ) pd.DataFrame({ "estimate": faces.estimate.round(3), "t": faces.stat.round(2), "p": faces.p_value.round(4), }) # voxels 0–4 recover ≈ 2.0 at p≈0; voxels 5–9 are null ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Coming from R / `fmrireg`? The R-style string formula still works and compiles to the *same* Spec tree — `fm.fmri_lm("hrf(condition)", dataset)` is exact sugar for `fm.fmri_lm(hrf("condition"), dataset)`. Prefer the typed form in Python: it is composable, IDE-introspectable, and inspectable before fitting. ::: ## Three promises {.promise-heading} ::: {.promise-grid} ::: {.promise-card} #### Typed HRFs, baselines, contrasts, AR options, single-trial estimators, and group reductions are inspectable Python values — constructed once, validated at the boundary. [Get started](get-started.qmd) [`hrf("condition")`]{.promise-tag} ::: ::: {.promise-card} #### Composable Terms compose with `+` into one typed design, and the same workflow — `fmri_dataset → fmri_lm → contrast → group` — carries it from data to group results, shown end to end with recovered numbers on the [golden path](tutorials/golden-path.qmd). [`hrf(...) + drift(...)`]{.promise-tag} ::: ::: {.promise-card} #### Parity-validated R behavior, Nilearn, and FitLins are treated as references; agreement is proven through checked-in benchmark and cross-testing artifacts. [Workflow overview](tutorials/overview-workflow.qmd) [`fm.design_matrix`]{.promise-tag} ::: ::: `fmrimod` is the unified Python home for the `fmri*` R modeling ecosystem — not a mechanical translation. The public API is redesigned around typed composition, reproducible analysis objects, and workflow parity checked against concrete artifacts.
